title.narrative: AWF- Biodiversity Conservation in Kenya's Southern Landscape

description.narrative:
African Wildlife Foundation (AWF) genomförde tillsammans med Indigenous Livelihood Enhancement Partners (ILEPA Kenya) och Land Development and Governance Institute (LDGI) en presentation för Kenya Development Section den 3 oktober 2022 om behovet av insatser för biologisk mångfaldsbevarande i det södra landskapet i Kenya. Presentationen fokuserade på att hantera förlusten av biologisk mångfald i landskapet, särskilt till följd av den återkommande torkan, den växande mänskliga befolkningen samt hotet från urbanisering, vilka har mycket allvarliga konsekvenser för både vilda djur och lokalsamhällenas försörjningsmöjligheter i Maasai Mara–Amboseli–Tsavo-ekosystemet, i de södra delarna av Kenya i Narok, Kajiado och Taita Taveta.
Resultat 1: Återställd, stärkt och skyddad biologisk mångfald för ökad klimatresiliens i produktiva och skyddande landskap.
Resultat 2: Förbättrade försörjningsmöjligheter för samhällen genom biodiversitetsbaserade företag och utvecklade värdekedjor.
Resultat 3: Stärkta och samordnade samhällsbaserade kunskapssystem samt nationella övervakningssystem för bevarande av biologisk mångfald.
Resultat 4: Förstärkt kapacitet på länsnivå för integrering av klimatförändringsperspektiv i länens policyer och planer för biologisk mångfald och miljö.
Resultat 5: Förbättrad styrning av gemensam mark för att stärka bevarandet och skyddet av biologisk mångfald, inklusive fördelar för rättighetsinnehavare.

African Wildlife Foundation (AWF) together with Indigenous Livelihood Enhancement Partners (ILEPA Kenya) and Land Development and Governance Institute (LDGI) made a presentation to the Kenya Development Section on 3rd October, 2022 on the need for response for biodiversity conservation in the Southern Landscape of Kenya to address biodiversity loss in the landscape especially due to the perennial drought, growing human population and threat of urbanisation impacting very heavily on wildlife as well as community livelihoods in the Maasai Mara­-Amboseli­-Tsavo ecosystem, in the southern landscape of Kenya in Narok, Kajiado and Taita Taveta.
Outcome 1: Restored, enhanced, and protected biodiversity for increased climate resilience in productive and protective landscapes Outcome 2: Improved livelihood of communities through biodiversity-­based enterprises and developed value chains Outcome 3: Strengthened and coordinated community­based knowledge and national monitoring systems for biodiversity conservation Outcome 4: Enhanced County capacity for climate change mainstreaming into County biodiversity and environmental policies and plans. Outcome 5: Enhanced governance of community land to strengthen biodiversity conservation and protections including benefits for rights holder

This project is implemented by partners' - African Wildlife Foundation (AWF) who are a major international conservation organization focused on protecting wildlife and habitats in Africa.
The focus of this contribution is on conserving and restoring Southern Kenya's ecosystems and their services to improve resilience, integrity, and connectivity to deliver sustainable and decent livelihoods.
An integrated approach to conservation, development, and human well-being will ensure that productive use of land and related resources are planned to safeguard and restore important critical productive assets and ecosystem services and bend the curve on biodiversity loss so that these ecosystems and biodiversity underpin sustainable inclusive socio-economic development and the well-being of the targeted communities.
The following objectives are pursued:
Objective 1: Restored, enhanced, and protected biodiversity for increased climate resilience in productive and protective landscapes Objective 2: Improved livelihood of communities through biodiversity-based enterprises and developed value chains Objective 3: Strengthened and Coordinated community-based knowledge and national monitoring systems for biodiversity conservation Objective 4: Enhanced County capacity for climate change mainstreaming into County biodiversity and environmental policies and plans Objective 5: Enhanced governance of community land to strengthen biodiversity conservation and protections including benefits for rights holders

title.narrative: Agreement AWF Enhancing Biodiversity Conservation and Climate resilience in Southern Kenya Landscape
Contribution agreement AWF Biodiv jointly with ILEPA-LDGI
Decision AWF Enhancing Biodiversity Conservation and Climate resilience in Southern Kenya Landscape

description.narrative:
Year 2 achieved strong ecological and community level outcomes, with progress in restoration, water security, livelihoods, and policy support. While audit, procurement, and environmental constraints shows some delays, these were managed through technical redesigns, strengthened partner coordination, and documentation of deviations.
The project is well positioned for accelerated delivery in Year 3 with corrective actions and The Embassy's approvals underway. Some unexpected but positive indirect outcomes included increased women and youth demonstrated stronger than anticipated leadership in natural resource management groups, indigenous Maasai Food Festival generated regional interest, enhancing cultural knowledge exchange and climate resilience dialogue, county level conservation governance shifts (e.g., Amboseli National Park management transition) created new partnership opportunities leveraged by the project.
Overall, the impactful results as per objective included:
1. Biodiversity Restoration & Protection Major Progress (67% of target achieved)
3,700.07 hectares of land have been restored, protected, or enhanced-representing 67% of the 5,519.93 ha project target. 104.71 ha restored through Farmer Managed Natural Regeneration (FMNR) by 98 farmers, strengthening drought resilience and reducing humanwildlife conflict. 2,482.48 ha of riparian, catchments, and wetlands protected through reactivated Water Resource Users Associations (WRUAs) and community stewardship. Water pans desilted and rehabilitated in Lumo, Maungu, and Tsavo East National Parknow critical wildlifelivestock water sources attracting elephants, giraffes and livestock daily, and reducing pressure on degraded areas. 800 households and over 5,000 livestock benefiting from rehabilitated springs in Naikara. 7000 tilapia fingerlings stocked in Lake Jipe fishponds, providing alternative livelihoods and reducing pressure on the lake.
2. Livelihoods & Nature Based Enterprises
Laying Strong Foundations, the project initiated key livelihood models that will scale significantly in Years 34. 143 households engaged in pasture production enterprises land leasing models developed to accelerate expansion. Beef production strengthened at Kasigau Ranch through livestock planning and staff training. Water access interventions (rock catchments, rooftop harvesting, village systems) designed to reach 4,000 beneficiaries. Strong partnerships with County Governments supporting tourism, conservation enterprises, and value-chain development. NB: Livelihood rollout was slower than planned due to land disputes, climate extremes, and shift from land purchase to leasing, but is now positioned for scale.
3. Community Knowledge & Monitoring Strengthened
Two biodiversity monitoring protocols developed and undergoing validation. Community balance scorecards launched across all three counties, revealing governance and landuse gaps and enabling targeted action. Digitization of Spatial Data Infrastructure initiated for Kajiado and Taita Taveta, improving evidence-based planning. Research assistants and technical county staff trained in environmental monitoring and GIS.
4. Climate Change Mainstreaming in County Policy
Climate considerations integrated into three major county plans: Taita Taveta spatial plan, Ndara B Land use plan & Amboseli Ecosystem land use plan 50 climate campaigns conducted - expanding public engagement and awareness. County officials trained on sustainable land management, climate adaptation and biodiversity governance. The historic transfer of Amboseli National Park to Kajiado County Government, with AWF serving as a key technical partner in ensuring ecological and community safeguards.
5. Community Land Governance & Benefit Sharing Improved
57% of community land areas in the project landscape now applying improved governance and biodiversity protection measures. 618 rights holders reporting increased access to benefits from conserved and protected areas. CLMCs and Land Control Boards trained on land-use planning, environmental management, and conflict resolution. Benefit sharing guidelines and investor engagement frameworks developed for Kasigau, Mbulia, Oza, and Tari B communities. Community sensitization on carbon markets conducted to protect communities from exploitative brokers.
The first year of implementation was marred by several challenges which contributed to delays in implementation. These included the early rains/EL Nino in October/November 2023, Gen-Z led demonstrations, limited budget lines, drought which affected restoration activities, delay in provision of requisite documents by Kenya Wildlife Service to equip the borehole in Tsavo East National Park, local politics in Narok that slowed implementation of forest conservation and low response by vendors in the procurement process.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
